stemMd: What is cos squared θ minus sin squared θ when θ=30 degrees?
explanationMd: At 30 degrees, cosine squared is 3/4 and sine squared is 1/4. Their difference is 1/2, also equal to cos60 degrees by the double-angle identity.

distractorRationale.d: This would be the sum of the squares.
distractorRationale.e: This is cos30 degrees, not the squared difference.
